title: Batch-vessel anti-windup strategies
equipment: Steam-heated batch vessel, temperature transmitter, and bounded steam control valve
physicalPurpose: Recover batch temperature after constrained heating without retaining unavailable steam-valve demand.
principalTechnique: No protection, control-signal clamping, back calculation, and combined anti-windup comparison
objective: Explain integral windup and direction, calculate tracking correction, and select anti-windup from measured recovery and actuator trade-offs rather than complexity.

simplifications: The vessel is represented by a local FOPDT temperature-deviation model.
The physical valve clamp is instantaneous and identical in all four runs.
Steam pressure, changing batch heat capacity, reaction heat, valve stiction and independent trips are omitted.

baseline.limitation: The PI controller accumulates unavailable demand because only the downstream valve clamp knows the physical limit.

change.decision: Give the unchanged shipped PI controller the real valve limits and compare its BackCalculation and Combined equations, using Tt=dt to realise signal clamping.

disturbances: Feed-temperature deviation remains fixed so strategy is the only changed cause

acceptance.window: complete unprotected run; subtract the synchronized applied steam-valve trim
unprotected recovery time minus each protected recovery time after 20 s restoration
each protected run after 20 s restoration
each protected run after 20 s restoration

abortPredicates: PV, applied MV or requested output is nonfinite
Applied valve trim leaves -3.5 to 3.5 percent
Plant, gains, limits, initial state or events differ between runs
safety.restorationMode: Restore zero-deviation SP, allow bounded recovery, then select Manual at 0 percent valve trim
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The unreachable demand and deliberately unprotected baseline must not be applied to a physical vessel without independent process/interlock review and immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain and compare no anti-windup, signal clamping, back calculation, and combined anti-windup using reproducible vessel evidence.

learning.context: Amplitude and rate constraints created requested/applied output gaps and exposed slow recovery caused by retained integral demand.
learning.reason: The controller must account for constrained output, but different anti-windup equations trade state correction, PV recovery and actuator movement differently.
theory: Windup is retained controller demand accumulated while the actuator cannot apply it; clipping only the final signal does not change that state.
Control-signal clamping is BackCalculation with tracking time equal to cycle time, making the correction coefficient dt/Tt equal one.
Ordinary BackCalculation subtracts dt/Tt times nominal minus saturated output, so Tt controls tracking speed.
Combined anti-windup blocks integral motion farther into saturation, permits integration away from the limit, and then back-calculates remaining saturation error.
learning.workedPrediction: For 10 percent saturation error, dt 0.1 s and Tt 3.25 s, BackCalculation removes 0.308 percent in one sample; Tt=dt removes the complete 10 percent gap.
practicalPreparation: Inspect the named vessel, transmitter, steam valve, feed-temperature disturbance, signal units, operating point, limits and zero-trim safe state.
Calculate both tracking corrections and confirm identical plant, PI controller, event, initial state and physical limit before four fresh approved simulation runs.
learning.baseline: Run strategy 0 with wide PI-controller limits and the same downstream -3.5 to 3.5 percent physical valve clamp to reproduce windup from Lessons 8 and 9.
learning.change: Repeat with strategy 1 signal clamping, strategy 2 BackCalculation at Tt 3.25 s and strategy 3 Combined at Tt 3.25 s, changing nothing else.
learning.comparison: Classify protected strategies from the declared recovery, post-return saturation and undershoot limits, then select shortest recovery; use complete-run valve travel and state-equation simplicity only for declared ties.
learning.validation: Verify recovery times of 20.0, 13.1, 2.7 and 9.2 s respectively, protected post-restoration upper-limit hold at most 0.1 s, protected undershoot at most 0.05 degree Celsius, finite values, safe restoration and applied trim within -3.5 to 3.5 percent.
learning.explanation: Explain each difference from conditional integration and tracking correction; ordinary BackCalculation is selected locally because it has the shortest recovery among eligible strategies, not because of its name or complexity.
learning.transfer: For another constrained loop, reproduce the failure, calculate dt/Tt, include amplitude and rate constraints, and select a strategy from equivalent evidence. This setpoint-restoration run does not prove disturbance rejection; Lesson 11 compares servo and regulatory objectives.
